{{nihongo|'''Kogaikuni Shrine'''|蚕養国神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Mutsu Province]].

[[File:Kogaikuni-jinja torii.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Torii}}]]
'''Kogaikuni Shrine''' (こがいくにじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine in Kogaimachi, {{ill|Aizuwakamatsu|Q237699|qid=Q237699}}, {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|Q71707|qid=Q71707}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}; under the modern ranking system, it was a {{ill|Q712534|lt=prefectural shrine}}. Its formal name is '''Kogaikuni Jinja''' (蠶養國神社), and it is also called '''Kogaigu'''. Its crest is the "Aizu Mitsu-aoi."<ref name="origin">Shrine origin record.</ref>

It is known as a shrine associated with sericulture.

=== Enshrined deities ===
The shrine enshrines the following three deities.<ref name="origin"/>
* {{ill|Ukemochi|Q2280323|qid=Q2280323|lt=Ukemochi-no-Okami}}
* {{ill|Wakumusubi|lt=Wakumusubi|UNKNOWN|qid=Q10921330|lt=Wakumusubi-no-Okami}}
* {{ill|Amaterasu|abstract|Q455602|ar|أماتيراسو|ary|أماطيراسو|az|Amaterasu|bcl|Amaterasu|be|Аматэрасу|be_x_old|Аматэрасу|bew|Amatérasu|bg|Аматерасу|ca|Amaterasu|cs|Amaterasu|da|Amaterasu|de|Amaterasu|el|Αματεράσου|eo|Amaterasu|es|Amaterasu|et|Amaterasu|eu|Amaterasu|fa|آماتراسو|fi|Amaterasu|fr|Amaterasu|gl|Amaterasu|he|אמטראסו|hi|अमातेरसु|hr|Amaterasu|hu|Amateraszu Ómikami|hy|Ամատերասու Օմիկամի|id|Amaterasu|it|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神|jv|Amaterasu|ka|ამატერასუ|ko|아마테라스 오미카미|la|Amaterasu|lb|Amaterasu|lt|Amaterasu|lv|Amaterasu|min|Amaterasu|ml|അമതേരസു|mni|ꯑꯃꯇꯦꯔꯁꯨ ꯑꯣꯃꯤꯀꯃꯤ|ms|Amaterasu|nl|Amaterasu|nn|Amaterasu|no|Amaterasu|or|ଆମାତେରାଶୁ|pa|ਆਮਾਤੇਰਸ|pl|Amaterasu|pt|Amaterasu|ro|Amaterasu|rsk|Аматерасу|ru|Аматэрасу|sco|Amaterasu|sh|Amaterasu|simple|Amaterasu Ōmikami|sk|Amaterasu Ómikami|sl|Amaterasu|sr|Аматерасу|su|Amaterasu|sv|Amaterasu|ta|அமதெரசு|th|อามาเตราซุ|tl|Amaterasu|tok|jan sewi suli Amatelasu|tr|Amaterasu|uk|Аматерасу|uz|Amaterasu|vi|Amaterasu|wuu|天照大神|zh|天照大神|zh_min_nan|Amaterasu|zh_yue|天照大神|qid=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu-Omikami}}

=== History ===
=== Foundation ===
According to shrine tradition, the shrine was founded in 811 (Konin 2).<ref name="origin"/>

In the ''{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}'' {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, no other official shrine bears the name "Kogaikuni," making this name unique to this shrine. Scholars have argued that its foundation was related to {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=sericulture}}, and that it may have reflected a central-government policy to promote sericulture in Aizu rather than merely local custom.{{Sfn|蚕養国神社（神々）|1984}} As background, the ''{{ill|Nihon Kōki|Q1077029|qid=Q1077029}}'' entry for November 8, 796 records that women from several provinces were dispatched to Mutsu for two years to teach sericulture techniques.{{Sfn|蚕養国神社（神々）|1984}}

=== Historical outline ===
In the ''Engishiki Jinmyocho'' compiled in 927 (Encho 5), the shrine is listed as "Kogaikuni Shrine" in Aizu District, {{ill|Mutsu Province|Q907389|qid=Q907389}}, and classified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}.{{Sfn|蚕養国神社（平凡社）|1993}} Of the Engishiki shrines in Aizu District, only Kogaikuni Shrine and {{ill|Isasumi Shrine|Q3155136|qid=Q3155136}} are listed.{{Sfn|蚕養国神社（平凡社）|1993}}

Although it is not clearly recorded in the official national histories, shrine tradition says it was elevated to an official shrine in the Jowa era (834-848) by petition of Fujiwara no Fujimaro, then Azechi and Commander of the Chinju-fu, and that shrine buildings were first established in 1011 by local officials including Ishibe Shosho Michihide.<ref name="origin"/> The buildings were later lost to warfare and declined, but were restored by {{ill|Hoshina Masayuki|Q837236|qid=Q837236}}, first lord of the {{ill|Aizu Domain|Q4389944|qid=Q4389944}}, who also confirmed an endowment of 20 koku.<ref name="origin"/> In 1743 the shrine rank was raised to Shoichii; after another fire in 1807, it was rebuilt in 1819 by the 8th lord, {{ill|Matsudaira Katataka|Q846200|qid=Q846200}}.<ref name="origin"/>

After the Meiji Restoration, in November 1876 (Meiji 9), it was listed as a prefectural shrine in the modern shrine ranking system.{{Sfn|明治神社誌料|1912}}

=== Precinct ===
The main sanctuary is in Oji-zukuri (also called Kumano-zukuri).<ref name="origin"/> Other structures include a heiden, haiden, shinsenjo, and kaguraden.<ref name="origin"/>

An old cherry tree standing before the haiden is said to be over 1,000 years old and 14 meters tall; it is especially called '''Minehari-zakura'''.<ref name="board">Precinct information board.</ref> Shrine tradition says it was planted when the shrine buildings were established in 1011.<ref name="board"/> It is designated a natural monument of Aizuwakamatsu City.<ref name="board"/>

=== Festivals ===
* Tsukinamisai (1st and 15th of each month)<ref>Festival list per shrine origin record.</ref>
* New Year's Day Festival (January 1)
* Hatsuuma Festival (first "horse" day of February)
* Oka Festival / Spring Grand Festival (April 19)
* Summer purification and chinowa rite (June 30)
* Grand Festival (August 1)
* Mikoshi procession (August 2)
* New Grain Thanksgiving Festival (November 23)
* Year-end purification (December 30)
